# Baruch Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_003_page_001.jpg

---

**1** O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, the soul in anguish and the troubled spirit cry out to you.

**2** Hear, O Lord, and have mercy, for you are a merciful God; and have mercy on us, because we have sinned before you.

**3** For you are enthroned forever, and we are perishing forever.

**4** O Lord Almighty, God of Israel, hear now the prayer of the dead of Israel and of the sons of those who sinned before you, who did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God, and so calamities have clung to us.

**5** Do not remember the iniquities of our fathers, but remember your hand and your name at this time,

**6** for you are the Lord our God, and we will praise you, O Lord.

**7** For this reason you put your fear into our hearts, that we should call upon your name; and we will praise you in our exile, for we have put away from our hearts all the iniquity of our fathers who sinned against you.

**8** See, we are today in our exile where you scattered us, to be a reproach and a curse and to be punished for all the iniquities of our fathers who departed from the Lord our God.

**9** Hear, O Israel, the commandments of life; give ear, to learn prudence.

**10** Why is it, O Israel? Why are you in the land of your enemies? You have grown old in a foreign land;

**11** you are defiled with the dead, you are reckoned with those who go down to Hades.

**12** You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom!

**13** If you had walked in the way of God, you would be dwelling in peace forever.

**14** Learn where there is wisdom, where there is strength, where there is understanding, that you may at the same time discern where there is length of days and life, where there is light for the eyes and peace.

**15** Who has found her place? And who has entered her storehouses?

**16** Where are the rulers of the nations, and those who lordly it over the beasts of the earth,

**17** those who made sport of the birds of heaven, those who hoarded silver and gold, in which people trust, and there is no end to their getting;

**18** those who worked silver and were anxious about it, and whose works are inscrutable?

**19** They have vanished and gone down to Hades, and others have arisen in their place.

**20** Younger men have seen the light and have lived upon the earth, but the way of knowledge they have not known,

**21** nor have they understood her paths, nor have their sons received her; she has been kept far from them.

**22** She has not been heard of in Canaan, nor has she been seen in Teman;

**23** the sons of Hagar who seek for understanding upon the earth, the merchants of Merran and Teman, the storytellers and the seekers of understanding — none of them have known the way of wisdom, nor have they remembered her paths.

**24** O Israel, how great is the house of God! And how vast is the territory of his possession!

**25** It is great and has no end, it is high and immeasurable.

**26** The giants were born there, who were famous of old, great in stature, skilled in war.

**27** God did not choose them, nor did he give them the way of knowledge;

**28** so they perished because they had no wisdom; they perished through their own foolishness.

**29** Who has gone up into heaven and taken her, and brought her down from the clouds?

**30** Who has gone over the sea and found her, and will bring her for fine gold?

**31** There is no one who knows her way or who thinks about her path.

**32** But the one who knows all things knows her; he found her by his understanding. The one who prepared the earth for eternity has filled it with four-footed animals.

**33** The one who sends forth the light, and it goes; he called it, and it obeyed him trembling.

**34** The stars shone in their watches and were glad; he called them, and they said, "Here we are!" They shone with gladness for him who made them.

**35** This is our God; no other can be compared to him.

**36** He found the whole way of knowledge, and gave her to his servant Jacob and to Israel his beloved.

**37** Afterward she appeared upon the earth and lived among mortals.

**38** She is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endures forever. All who hold her fast will live, and those who forsake her will die.

---
*EMET notes: v.37 is the theological climax of the hymn and one of the most significant verses in the Deuterocanon. Greek: "meta touto en tē gē ōphthē kai en tois anthrōpois synanestraphē." The verb synanestraphē = she mixed with / conversed with / lived among. Christian tradition (especially in the Western church, cited by many Fathers) reads this as a prophecy of the Incarnation. The EMET renders it with strict literalism to preserve the theological range. v.23 "storytellers" for muthologan; "Merran" preserved as text reads.*
